ai.description: *Cnemaspis wynadensis* is a small gecko (SVL ~40 mm) with a brown dorsum featuring distinct yellow-orange spots. It is identified by a prominent precloacal pore and a lack of keeled scales on the venter.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cnemaspis wynadensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous series of enlarged, spine-like tubercles along its flanks, which are absent in most similar congeners.
ai.habitat: The Wynad Day Gecko inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found on tree trunks or rocks at altitudes between 700 and 1,100 meters.
ai.behavior: The Wynad Day Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects on rock surfaces and tree trunks within its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis wynadensis* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between June and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Wynad Day Gecko is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily found in the Wayanad region of Kerala and adjacent areas of Karnataka at moderate elevations.
